rationales.authenticity: Proper Irish terms (Máire Ní Chonail, sídhe), respect for local tradition, realistic wariness about 'the Good People'—all period-apt.
rationales.character: Brigid corrects the term 'Cailleach,' names the woman specifically, shows measured familiarity with herbalists and the fairy tradition—nuanced and authoritative.
rationales.craft: Longer than 2–4 sentences (4 full sentences) but justified by the richness; voice is steady and thoughtful.
rationales.language: Fluent code-switching between English and Irish, well-formed prose, 'Good People' is the idiom for fairy folk.
rationales.responsiveness: Directly answers who Máire is and what Brigid knows; explains her relationship to the fairy fort.
